correctness.rationale: For 0<c<1 project any optimizer to the two-dimensional ray span, then align the phases to increase one expectation while preserving the other. Write G_p(theta)=(cos^(2p)(theta)+cos^(2p)(gamma-theta))/2, gamma=arccos c, theta in [0,gamma]. On 0<theta<gamma/2 derivative sign equals sign(F(theta)-(2p-1)) where F is the positive log ratio of sines to cosines. The ratio is a strictly decreasing weighted mean of cot(s)cot(gamma-s), from +infinity to (1+c)/(1-c), hence the exact one/two-ray threshold c=1-1/p and uniqueness of off-center stationary solution. At c=0 and p=1 all rays in the projector span maximize, at c=0,p>1 only two projector rays, c=1 only common ray. Independent symbolic differentiation confirms the p=2 rational branches agree C1 but have second derivatives 19/2 versus 1/2 at c=1/2; finite grid source checks are not a continuum proof.
